title: Tool-poisoning demonstration exfiltrates WhatsApp history through an MCP-connected agent
summary: Researchers demonstrated that an AI agent connected to an open-source WhatsApp MCP server can be turned against its user. In one experiment a second, malicious MCP server changed its tool description after installation so the agent rerouted messages and sent the user's chat history to an attacker's number. In a second experiment, instructions hidden in an incoming WhatsApp message hijacked the agent when it listed chats. This is a research demonstration, not a reported compromise of real users.
attack_vector: MCP tool poisoning (a tool description changed after approval) and prompt injection through message content
root_cause: Agents trust tool descriptions and tool output from every connected server in one shared context, with no isolation between servers
impact: Showed that a user's whole message history and contact list can leave through the legitimate messaging channel, bypassing end-to-end encryption and traditional DLP
